channel.title: Global Supply Chain Bulletin
channel.description: An independent daily briefing on supply chains, energy transition and trade geopolitics.

item.title: Issue 113 — A seafarer is killed in a Gulf tanker attack as Iran's nuclear proposal to the US via Qatar stalls, Reuters reports
item.description: Reuters, gCaptain, Deutsche Welle and Seatrade Maritime report a seafarer was killed in a suspected missile attack on a tanker in the Gulf on Nov. 6, as Brent crude eased to $97.76; Al Arabiya separately notes Iran's Nov. 5 nuclear proposal to the US via Qatar remains unanswered.

item.title: Issue 112 — Iran sent a nuclear proposal to the US via Qatar as Brent crude rebounds to $99 a barrel, Reuters and Al Arabiya report
item.description: Hellenic Shipping News, Al Jazeera and Al Arabiya report Iran's Revolutionary Guard navy claimed five tankers and a tugboat caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz on Nov. 5, as Brent crude rebounded to $99.20 a barrel; Reuters and Al Arabiya separately report Iran sent a nuclear proposal to the US via Qatar.

item.title: Issue 111 — Brent crude falls below $100 a barrel; hopes rise for a US-Iran peace deal after Democrats' midterm win, FT and Al Arabiya report
item.description: The Financial Times, Economic Times and Al Arabiya report Brent crude fell under $100 a barrel on Nov. 4; a US-Iran peace deal looked more likely after Democrats' midterm win, as Mining Weekly and MINING.COM report Freeport-McMoRan approved a $4.5 billion expansion of its Bagdad, Arizona copper mine.

item.title: Issue 110 — US strikes Iran's Qeshm Island near the Strait of Hormuz, Reuters and Livemint report
item.description: MINING.COM and Bloomberg report Congo seized thousands of tons of copper and cobalt in a crackdown on illegal mining, as Livemint and the Associated Press report India's Navy freed 20 Iranian crew from a Somali pirate-hijacked fishing vessel after a 48-hour operation.

item.title: Issue 109 — US strikes Iran's Qeshm Island near the Strait of Hormuz, Reuters and Livemint report
item.description: Reuters and Livemint report Brent rose to $104.92 a barrel after a US strike on Iran's Qeshm Island, according to Reuters, as the Associated Press and Al Arabiya separately report Khamenei warned any new US or Israeli attack would draw a response with no 'geographic limits.'

item.title: Issue 108 — Iran's Guard says two more tankers exploded in the Strait of Hormuz as Washington again withholds comment
item.description: Reuters and Al Jazeera report Iran's Revolutionary Guard navy now says two more tankers exploded in the Strait of Hormuz, a day after gCaptain and Al Arabiya reported its tally had risen to four, as Washington's CENTCOM has not commented on the new claim.

item.title: Issue 107 — Iran's Guard says four tankers now on fire in the Strait of Hormuz as Washington again rejects its mine account
item.description: gCaptain, Al Arabiya, Euronews and Times of Israel report Iran's Revolutionary Guard navy now says four tankers have caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz, up from the three it reported a day earlier, as Washington's CENTCOM continues to reject Iran's mine account.

item.title: Issue 106 — Tanker in the Strait of Hormuz hit by limpet mines, UKMTO says, as Iran's Guard reports three vessels on fire
item.description: Reuters and gCaptain report a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz was hit by limpet mines on Oct. 30, UKMTO says, as Iran's Revolutionary Guard separately claims three tankers caught fire; Al Arabiya carries both accounts and Washington has not commented.

item.title: Issue 105 — Iran's Hormuz authority threatens Sinokor tankers with legal action from Nov. 1, Reuters reports
item.description: Deutsche Welle and Al Arabiya report a ship caught fire near the Strait of Hormuz on Oct. 29 as Iran's Nov. 1 deadline for Sinokor's tanker fleet approaches, with IMF PortWatch's latest count holding transits near 3.3 a day.

item.title: Issue 104 — Iran's Hormuz authority threatens Sinokor tankers with legal action from Nov. 1, Reuters reports
item.description: Euronews and Reuters report Europe's benchmark gas price crossed €100 per megawatt-hour on Oct. 28 for the first time since the 2022 crisis, as EU energy chief Dan Jørgensen warned of a difficult winter.

item.title: Issue 103 — Iran's Hormuz authority threatens Sinokor tankers with legal action from Nov. 1, Reuters reports
item.description: Reuters, gCaptain and Seatrade Maritime report Iran's Strait Authority will take legal action against Sinokor's tanker fleet in the Strait of Hormuz from Nov. 1, while Al Arabiya and Nikkei Asia report a Saudi-led coalition continues intercepting Houthi missiles aimed at Riyadh.

item.title: Issue 102 — Iran claims control of Strait of Hormuz, warns US warships against entry, Livemint reports
item.description: Al Arabiya and Nikkei Asia report a Saudi-led coalition continues intercepting Houthi missiles aimed at Riyadh, while the Associated Press and Livemint report many Iranians now fear a return to all-out war once US midterm and Israeli elections pass.

item.title: Issue 101 — Iran claims control of Strait of Hormuz, warns US warships against entry, Livemint reports
item.description: Al Arabiya and Nikkei Asia report a Saudi-led coalition downed more than 10 Houthi missiles aimed at Riyadh on Oct. 25, while Reuters reports the kingdom's main airport reopened only partially; Trading Economics puts Brent at $115.24 a barrel Monday, off Friday's six-month high.

item.title: Issue 100 — Iran claims control of Strait of Hormuz, warns US warships against entry, Livemint reports
item.description: Brent crude held near $116.72 a barrel Friday, up over 3% on the week per Trading Economics, as Livemint and Reuters reported Iran now claims to control the Strait of Hormuz and is warning US warships to stay out of the Gulf.

item.title: Issue 99 — Iran's IRGC says seven vessels hit mines near Hormuz, threatens US bases over tanker escorts
item.description: Nikkei Asia and Euronews report an oil spill hit UAE beaches as tanker attacks multiplied near Hormuz, sending Brent to $116.91 a barrel, up 3.30% and its highest since April, per Trading Economics.

item.title: Issue 98 — Iran's IRGC says seven vessels hit mines near Hormuz, threatens US bases over tanker escorts
item.description: Reuters, Al Jazeera and Al Arabiya report Iran's IRGC Navy says seven vessels struck mines near Hormuz and threatens the US, as IMF PortWatch shows transits still at 3.7 a day, a fraction of 2023 levels.

item.title: Issue 97 — UK to send Typhoon jets on defensive missions to shield Saudi Arabia from Houthi attacks
item.description: Euronews and Al Jazeera report Britain’s Typhoon jets will fly defensive missions over Saudi Arabia, as IMF PortWatch shows Bab-el-Mandeb transits holding near 26.4 a day, about a third of 2023 levels, with no Houthi response reported.

item.title: Issue 96 — Trump's Russia sanctions waiver draws instant bipartisan backlash in Congress
item.description: Euronews and Al Jazeera report Britain will fly Typhoon jets on defensive missions to shield Saudi Arabia from Houthi attacks, as IMF PortWatch shows Bab-el-Mandeb transits near 26.4 a day, about a third of 2023 levels.

item.title: Issue 95 — Trump's Russia sanctions waiver draws instant bipartisan backlash in Congress
item.description: Axios, AP and Business Standard report Trump's Oct 16 Russia sanctions waiver kept drawing bipartisan anger into Oct 19, with Brent crude slipping to $108.17 a barrel on expectations of more Russian fuel reaching market before steadying near $110 Oct 20 (Trading Economics).

item.title: Issue 94 — Trump's Russia sanctions waiver draws instant bipartisan backlash in Congress
item.description: Axios and Business Standard report Trump's Oct 16 waiver of new Russia sanctions drew instant bipartisan anger in Congress, with Rubio telling Al Arabiya and Reuters a permanent decision could take up to 60 days.

item.title: Issue 93 — Trump waives new Russia and Iran sanctions days before the October 18 deadline, citing national interest
item.description: The Associated Press, Axios and Deutsche Welle report Trump waived new Russia and Iran sanctions just two days before their Oct 18 deadline, citing the national interest, while Reuters and Bloomberg report the Bank of Canada warned of sharply higher inflation as oil prices surge.

item.title: Issue 92 — Africa Finance Corporation eyes iron-ore and uranium investments as South Africa launches a $541 million rail upgrade
item.description: Africa Finance Corporation is targeting fresh iron-ore and uranium financing across the continent as South Africa's Transnet began a $541 million upgrade of its iron-ore export railway, Mining Weekly, Mining.com.au and Ecofin Agency report, while major container carriers signal a full return to the Suez Canal by the first quarter of 2027, Hellenic Shipping News and Seatrade Maritime report.

item.title: Issue 91 — IMF warns Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia could worsen its economic contraction after Aramco HQ strike
item.description: Houthi missiles killed several officials in a strike on Yemen's Aden presidential palace Thursday, Reuters, Deutsche Welle, Al Jazeera and the South China Morning Post report, as the IMF's pre-strike forecast already puts Saudi Arabia's 2026 GDP contraction at 3.3% after missiles hit Aramco's Dhahran headquarters, Euronews, Bloomberg and the Associated Press report.

item.title: Issue 90 — Fuel delivery delays trigger panic buying and hour-long queues across Bali
item.description: Indonesia's resort island of Bali faced hour-long fuel queues and panic buying on Oct 14, Africanews, Euronews and the Straits Times report, as Nikkei Asia reports the shortage has spread to other regions with pump prices climbing.

item.title: Issue 89 — France boards another Russia-linked 'shadow fleet' tanker; Moscow calls it 'piracy'
item.description: The Financial Times and Bloomberg report a strike hit Saudi Aramco's Riyadh headquarters, unconfirmed by Saudi authorities, as Riyadh's cabinet vowed Houthis will face 'consequences' and Turkey's Erdogan pledged support, Al Arabiya and the Times of Israel report.

item.title: Issue 88 — Saudi-led coalition intercepts a Houthi missile at Riyadh as airlines scrap more Saudi flights
item.description: Iran's foreign ministry said it needs more time to answer Washington's counter-offer on reopening the Strait of Hormuz, Reuters and Al Arabiya report, a day after Tehran called the earlier US reply 'insufficient'.

item.title: Issue 87 — Iran says the US response to its Hormuz reopening plan was 'insufficient'
item.description: Iran's security chief called Washington's response to its Hormuz reopening plan "insufficient," gCaptain, Al Arabiya and Reuters report, as US forces disabled another cargo vessel breaching Iran shipping limits.

item.title: Issue 86 — Taiwan earmarks a record NT$1.1 trillion for its 2027 defense budget
item.description: Taiwan earmarked a record NT$1.1 trillion for its 2027 defense budget, citing deterrence, Deutsche Welle and the Straits Times report, after President Trump pressed Taipei to pay more for US protection.

item.title: Issue 85 — Magnitude 7.7 earthquake strikes Panama near the canal route, triggering tsunami warnings
item.description: A magnitude 7.6-7.7 earthquake struck Panama near the canal route on Friday, triggering tsunami warnings across six countries and an airport evacuation, MercoPress, the Associated Press, CBC News, Al Jazeera and Euronews report, with no confirmed canal disruption yet.

item.title: Issue 84 — US imposes fresh sanctions on tankers in Iran's shadow fleet
item.description: The US Treasury sanctioned more tankers and firms tied to Iran's shadow fleet as Strait of Hormuz transits fell to their lowest level in over two months, Reuters, gCaptain, Al Arabiya, the Hindu and Business Standard report, while Secretary of State Rubio said Iran has "lost complete control" of the strait.
